This push toward formal verification is precisely the maturation point the AI revolution needed in pure mathematics. We must assess the formal language limitations and the potential attack vectors within the verification agents themselves. Until the operational cost and time complexity for verifying proofs of increasing size are quantified, this remains a specialized niche tool rather than a universally viable system for mathematical truth.

AI-generated proofs are the mathematical equivalent of a massive, untested PR submitted by a colleague who 'just knows it works.'
